transcript.en: My topic is handedness-whether in different sports it is better to be left or right-sided or whether a more balanced approach is more successful.
transcript.zh: 我的题目是用手习惯，在不同的运动中，左撇子、右撇子或是两手配合，哪种更容易成功？

transcript.en: I'm left-handed myself and I actually didn't see any relevance to my own life when I happened to start reading an article by a sports psychologist called Peter Matthews.
transcript.zh: 我是左撇子，在我看体育心理学家皮特·马修斯写的文章时，我没觉得这和我的生活有什么关系。

transcript.en: He spent the first part of the article talking about handedness in music instead of sport, which I have to say almost put me off from reading further.
transcript.zh: 他在文章的第一部分写的是用手习惯在音乐中的影响，而不是体育，我不得不说这几乎让我没能读下去。

transcript.en: But what I soon became struck by was the sheer volume of both observation and investigation he had done in many different sports and I felt persuaded that what he had to say  would be of real interest.
transcript.zh: 但是我很快惊讶于他在各种体育运动的大量观察和调查，我开始相信他说的话肯定有意思。

transcript.en: I think Matthews' findings will be beneficial, not so much in helping sportspeople to work on their weaker side,
transcript.zh: 我认为马修斯的调查很有用，不是帮助运动员克服他们的弱点，

transcript.en: but more that they can help them identify the most suitable strategies to use in a given game.
transcript.zh: 而是帮助他们认识到在比赛中最适合的战略。

transcript.en: Although most trainers know how important handedness is, at present they are rather reluctant to make use of the insights scientists like Matthews can give, which I think is rather short-sighted
transcript.zh: 尽管多数训练员知道用手习惯的重要性，但是他们目前却迟迟不利用马修斯这种科学家提出的观点，我认为这是目光短浅的。

transcript.en: because focusing on individual flexibility is only part of the story.
transcript.zh: 因为关注个人的灵活性只是体育的一部分。

transcript.en: Anyway, back to the article.
transcript.zh: 总之，回到文章中。

transcript.en: Matthews found a German study which looked at what he called  mixed-handedness: that is the capacity to use both left and right hands equally.
transcript.zh: 马修斯发现一项德国研究，他称之为“双手并用”。换句话说就是同等的使用左右手的能力。

transcript.en: It looked at mixed-handedness in 40 musicians on a variety of instruments.
transcript.zh: 它着眼于40名音乐家对待各种乐器时的双手并用。

transcript.en: Researchers examined a number of variables, for example, type of instrument played, regularity of practice undertaken and length of time playing instrument...
transcript.zh: 研究者调查了许多因素。例如，乐器类型、演奏的规律性、演奏的时长……

transcript.en: and found the following: keyboard players had high levels of mixed-handedness, whereas string players like cellists and violinists strongly favoured one hand.
transcript.zh: 结果发现键盘演奏者的双手并用能力高，而弦乐演奏者更偏好使用一只手，如大提琴家和小提琴家。

transcript.en: Also those who started younger were more mixed-handed.
transcript.zh: 此外，那些初学年龄更小的人，双手并用的情况更为普遍 。

transcript.en: Matthews also reports studies handedness in apes.
transcript.zh: 马修斯还调查了猿猴的用手习惯。

transcript.en: Apes get a large proportion of their food by 'fishing' ants from ant hills. The studies show that apes, like humans, show handedness - though for them right - and left -handedness is about equal, whereas about 85 per cent of humans are right-handed.
transcript.zh: 猿猴可以从蚂蚁山中找到大量的蚂蚁作为食物。调查表明猿猴和人类一样的用手习惯，尽管它们可以平均的使用左右手，然而85%的人类是右撇子。

transcript.en: Studies showed that apes consistently using the same hand fished out 30% more ants than those varying between the two.
transcript.zh: 调查显示猿猴不停地使用同一只手可以比两手并用多抓到30%的蚂蚁。

transcript.en: Matthews started researching several different sports and found different types of handedness in each.
transcript.zh: 马修斯开始调查几种不同的体育项目，并发现每种都有不同类型的用手习惯。

transcript.en: By the way, he uses "handedness" to refer to the dominant side for feet and eyes as well as hands.
transcript.zh: 顺便说一下，他用“用手习惯”来指代脚、眼和手的优势侧‌‌。

transcript.en: Anyway, his team measured the hand, feet, and eyes of 2,611 players
transcript.zh: 总之，他的团队测试了2611名参与者的手、脚和眼。

transcript.en: and found that there were really three main types of laterality: mixed — you work equally well on both sides — both hand and eye; single — you tend to favour one side
transcript.zh: 并发现了三种主要的侧重类型。混合型，手和眼，两边的使用率平均。单一型，你往往喜欢用一边。

transcript.en: but both hand and eye favour the same side; and cross-laterality - a player's hands and eyes favour only one side but they are opposite sides.
transcript.zh: 但是手和眼都在同一边。交叉侧重型，参与者的手和眼只喜欢用一边，但是它们是对立的两边。

transcript.en: Let's start with hockey.
transcript.zh: 让我们先从曲棍球说起。

transcript.en: Matthews found that it was best to be mixed-handed - this is because a hockey stick must be deployed in two directions - it would be a drawback to have hand or eye  favouring one side.
transcript.zh: 马斯特发现这项运动最适合混合型选手，因为曲棍球球棍必须从两面挥出，只喜欢用手或眼的一面是不利的。

transcript.en: An interesting finding is that mixed-handed hockey players  were significantly more confident  than their single-handed counterparts.
transcript.zh: 一项有趣的发现是左右手分工的曲棍球选手比他们的单手型对手更自信。

transcript.en: Things are slightly different in racket sports like tennis.
transcript.zh: 在球拍类运动上有点不同，比如网球。

transcript.en: Here the important thing is to have the dominant hand and eye on the one side.
transcript.zh: 在这里最重要的是有一方手和眼的主导面。

transcript.en: This means that there is a bigger area of vision on the side where most of the action occurs.
transcript.zh: 这意味着在多数运动发生的那一侧有更大的视觉空间。

transcript.en: If a player is cross lateral the racket is invisible from the dominant eye for much of the swing.
transcript.zh: 如果选手是交叉侧重型，那么球拍由于大幅摆动，在主视野中不可见。

transcript.en: It means that they can only make corrections much later...and often the damage has been done by then.
transcript.zh: 这意味着他们只能延迟更正，并且他们经常会造成损害。

transcript.en: And moving to a rather different type of sport which involves large but precise movements — gymnastics.
transcript.zh: 然后是一项不同类型的体育，它需要大量而精确的动作——体操。

transcript.en: It's been found that cross hand-eye favouring is best.
transcript.zh: 交叉用手、用眼是最好的。

transcript.en: The predominant reason for this is because it aids balance - which is of course absolutely central to performance in this sport.
transcript.zh: 主要的原因是能够帮助保持平衡，这绝对是这项体育中最重要的。
